T-01.name: Houthi CDF ASCM launch position (hide sites 1-3)
T-01.location: Ras Isa peninsula, al-Salif district, al-Hudaydah governorate
T-01.function: Coastal-defense anti-ship cruise missile launch / TEL hide sites
T-01.unit: Houthi Coastal Defense Forces (CDF), 2nd Coastal Missile Bde (assessed)
T-01.effect: Destroy TELs and hide-site revetments; deny launch from Ras Isa

intel.text: Source observed two large flatbed trucks with tarp-covered rectangular loads, escorted by two technicals, moving south from al-Mansuriyah towards Ras Isa at approximately 0215 local, 06 Oct. Trucks turned off the coastal road near the oil terminal approach, heading into the dune area west of the road. Convoy did not have visible markings. Source states similar movements occur weekly, typically Tue/Thu nights. Loads assessed as missile transporter vehicles based on size and escort pattern.

Three revetted hide sites identified (DPIs in MSS object). Sites consist of sandbag-covered revetments cut into dune faces, each with tire tracks leading to hardened access paths. One TEL-sized vehicle partially visible under camouflage net at center site during 08 Oct pass. No permanent structures within 1.2 km; nearest civilian housing cluster at 2.8 km southeast near al-Salif village. Zero civilian activity observed near sites.

Net 14 (callsigns 'Lighthouse' and 'Torch') observed active 22 Jul and 09 Sep. Net re-energized 05-08 Oct with periodic traffic. Short duration encrypted bursts, followed by single-word acknowledgments from 'Lighthouse' to 'Torch'. Bursts correlate with vehicle movement times observed via other sources. On 09 Oct, net transmitted a 4-character grid repeated three times, then silenced. Likely launch-coordination net for CDF 2nd Coastal Missile Bde. No personal identifiers captured.

Between 08-13 Oct, nightly activity at hide sites 1-3: vehicle lights visible departing sites 1 and 2 between 2200-2300, returning 0300-0400. Site 3 remains dark, likely static launch site. One TEL-sized vehicle moves between site 2 and site 1 at 0115 on alternate nights. No daytime activity observed except occasional single personnel walking perimeter. All movement ceases by dawn. No civilian vehicles approach within 1 km of hide sites.

T-02.name: Coastal surveillance radar site
T-02.function: Surface-search radar and EO mast providing targeting data for ASCM / USV attacks
T-02.unit: Houthi CDF / naval forces surveillance detachment
T-02.effect: Destroy radar antenna, generator and ops shelter

intel.text: Source with access to Houthi CDF naval logistics at al-Hudaydah reports radar site on northern Kamaran Island non-operational for 36 hours due to generator failure. Replacement generator expected via dhow within 72 hours. Also reports detachment personnel rotate every third day, with handover occurring at evening prayer time. Source notes site commander prioritizes radar repair over EO mast, citing need to track Saudi-linked vessels near Bab al-Mandeb.

Site on low ridge 450m west-northwest of first dwelling in fishing village. Antenna mast, two shelters, and generator confirmed. Radar antenna visible at 20m height, orientated southwest toward Red Sea shipping lane. Generator shows no heat signature at 0900Z, consistent with reported downtime. No visible personnel. Vehicle tracks between site and village, with fresh tire marks along coastal trail. Village civilian vessels moored in bay, no military equipment observed.

X-band surface-search radar emissions intercepted on carrier frequency 9410 MHz with 0.1 microsecond pulse. Emissions logged on 11 of 14 nights, intermittent during daylight. Associated UHF voice net active between site and dhow callsign 'KAMAR-7', passing bearing and range data to command ashore. Net controls radar off/on status. Call sign rotation observed every 4-5 hours, likely shift change. No emitter activity 0600-1200 local on 08-09 Oct.

Overnight activity: radar emissions and generator exhaust begin at 2100Z, cease around 0400Z. Small vehicle arrives at site 1830Z most nights, departs 0600Z. Two personnel visible outside shelters during relief rotation. Daytime: site minimal activity; no emissions between 0600-1500Z. Village fishing boats routinely transit within 300m of site perimeter but no interaction observed. No visible guards; no lights at site after 2300Z. Generator tested briefly at 1500Z on four of six nights.

T-03.name: Explosive USV staging pier and boat shed
T-03.location: Small-boat harbor, al-Salif port, al-Hudaydah governorate
T-03.function: Assembly and launch point for explosive-laden uncrewed surface vessels (WBIED)
T-03.effect: Destroy boat shed, staged USVs and fueling point

intel.text: Source, a former fisherman, reports security personnel have barred all local boats from the small-boat harbor pier since August. He observed a corrugated shed at the south end being used for boat work. Two small fiberglass boats with cameras on masts were seen entering the shed at night. Personnel wear civilian clothes, no uniforms. He heard loud engine tests after midnight. Source is reliable, reporting firsthand.

Imagery of al-Salif small-boat harbor, south end, shows a corrugated metal boat shed (approx. 25x12m) and an adjacent floating pier. Two fiberglass hulls, 6-8m, with mast-mounted cameras are visible alongside the pier, consistent with WBIEDs. A third hull is partially inside the shed. Commercial port warehouse observed 150m north; cluster of fishermen's huts 260m east. No recent activity on date of collection.

Intercepted maritime C2 net, callsign 'SKIPPER', active on UHF. Multiple stations, including one collocated with al-Salif harbor area, exchanged position and status updates. Traffic referenced 'boats ready' and 'waiting for order.' Correlated with the 19 Sep USV attack. Net active daily, peak hours after local midnight.

Over six nights of observation, activity at the south pier occurs predominantly between 2200 and 0400 local. Two or three individuals move between the shed and pier, occasionally conducting engine starts. Small boats are pulled alongside the pier, and at times a crane is used. Daytime activity minimal, limited to one guard. No civilian fishing boats approach the pier.

T-04.name: UAS launch and recovery site
T-04.location: Coastal plain 3 km N of Dhubab, Ta'izz governorate (Houthi-held since Sep 2026)
T-04.function: One-way-attack UAS launch rails, recovery strip and storage containers
T-04.effect: Destroy launch rails, storage containers and ground control shelter

intel.source: YM-HS-1014 (B2, established access, has proven reliable in past reporting)
intel.text: Source observed three flatbed trucks of 'aircraft parts' arrive at the coastal site 3 km N Dhubab from Ta'izz city. Offloading occurred at the four ISO containers under the direction of a UAF (Houthi Unmanned Air Force) officer. Source confirms the launch rails are positioned parallel to the shoreline, oriented toward the southwest. No personnel movements noted outside the cordoned area. Source assessed the site as fully operational for OWA (one-way-attack) launches.

Site shows a graded dirt strip approximately 250 m in length. Two launch rails (likely crated or semi-fixed) located at the eastern end of the strip. Four ISO containers are positioned in an L-shape adjacent to the western edge of the strip, partially sandbagged. Confirmed the presence of two airframes with swept wings on trailers near the containers, consistent with Shahed-type variants. A farm compound is visible 160 m west; no personnel or vehicles observed within the compound during this pass. No new construction since the last assessment.

Detected UAS ground-control datalink emissions from the target site. Net identified on VHF/UHF frequencies, callsign 'COASTAL' consistent with previous launch site activity. Three separate bursts of datalink activity, each lasting 15-20 minutes, were followed by a hiatus period. The net went silent immediately after each burst, likely during launch. No other traffic on regional nets. The same callsign was previously logged over Al Hudaydah in a separate operation. Senior-level coordination net remained quiet throughout the period.

Nightly activity follows a clear pattern. Between 1900-2200 local, two trucks arrive and position near the launch rails; a team of 6-10 personnel conduct pre-launch checks. Between 2300 and 0100, a single ground-control vehicle approaches the east end and remains stationary for 30-60 minutes. Launches occur within that window, usually 2-3 per night. Post-launch, personnel and vehicles return to the ISO containers. After 0200, the site is completely quiet. The farm compound to the west remains dark and inactive each night; no vehicles or personnel observed moving between the compound and the site.

T-05.name: ASCM / USV component storage warehouse
T-05.location: al-Hali district, Hodeidah port-adjacent industrial zone, al-Hudaydah
T-05.function: Storage and assembly of anti-ship missile and USV components (hardened warehouse)
T-05.unit: Houthi CDF logistics (assessed); Military Industrialization Authority support

intel.text: Source reports that since late August the former fishing-gear warehouse on the east side of the al-Hali industrial lane has been used by Houthi coastal-defense logistics personnel. Crates marked as 'pumps' are delivered by night in covered trucks; source observed missile fin sections and USV outboard motors through the open door on 06 Oct. 3-4 armed guards at the gate at all hours.

Hardened single-story warehouse (approx. 45 x 20 m), reinforced roof added since July. Two covered cargo trucks backed to loading door. Guard post at gate. Open-air fish market 140 m NW (stalls, ice trucks, boat landing). Residential 4-story block 90 m S. Mosque 170 m W. Fuel station 230 m N.

Houthi CDF logistics net: callsign associated with the al-Hali site coordinated 'delivery of the long items' to Ras Isa on 03 and 11 Oct. Handset geolocation places the logistics coordinator at the warehouse on 7 of the last 10 days (CEP 150 m). Corroborates HUMINT.

intel.source: MQ-9 FMV / persistent EO, 10 nights observed
intel.text: Night (2200-0300L): market empty except 2-6 ice-truck drivers sleeping in cabs; residential block lit until ~0100L. 0300-0330L: first fishing boats return on 6 of 10 nights, 5-15 people at boat landing by 0330L; on Thursdays traders arrive from ~0300L. 0400-0600L: market at full activity (150-250 people). Fajr prayer ~0445L.

T-06.name: Weapons storage tunnel entrances (portals 2 and 4)
T-06.function: Underground storage for missiles and UAS; portal and ventilation shaft
T-06.unit: Houthi missile forces / Military Industrialization Authority
T-06.effect: Collapse portals 2 and 4; deny access to storage galleries

intel.text: Source observed two flatbed trucks offloading crated missiles at portal 2 during the night of 29 Sep. Cargo was moved directly into tunnel. No activity at portal 4 observed on that date. Trucks had no markings; escorts in civilian pickup trucks. Source states repairs to both portals are complete and new blast doors are operational. Movement is sporadic, typically after midnight.

Imagery of Jebel Nuqum western face. Portal 2 and 4 show new steel blast doors, closed. Fresh gravel grading on approach ramp. Four light vehicles parked near portal 2. No visible surface-to-air systems. Nearest residential cluster identified at 420 m downslope east of portal 4; no construction or blast walls between residences and portal. Night-time imagery (SAR) shows heat signature at portal entrance.

Intercept of logistics net linked to missile force. Net active from 2100 to 0300 locally. Callsigns 'Falcon' and 'Gate' coordinated truck movement to coordinates matching Jebel Nuqum portal 2. Transmission reported 'delivery complete' at 0122Z. No direct coordination with higher HQ observed. Net dormant during daylight hours on all monitored days since 01 Oct.

Over six consecutive nights, average of 3 vehicles per night arrived at portal 2 between 2300 and 0200. Portal 4 used once, on 11 Oct. Security personnel (typically 4 to 6) visible on roof above portal 2. No civilian movement near site after 2200. Daytime activity limited to one guard post at each portal. No changes following recent shipping attacks.

T-07m.name: Houthi coastal-defense forward command post
T-07m.location: Former port police compound, Mocha (al-Mukha), Ta'izz governorate
T-07m.function: Forward C2 for Houthi coastal-defense and UAS units on the Bab al-Mandab coast
T-07m.effect: Destroy C2 building and communications mast

intel.text: Two independent sources report senior Houthi CDF officers using the former port police compound in Mocha since mid-September. Compound functions as forward C2 for coastal-defense and UAS units. Officers arrive/depart in white Toyota Land Cruisers. Staff seen carrying VHF radios and maps of Bab al-Mandab. Sources do not report activity at the nearby port administration building. Compound is walled, with main gate on north side.

Commercial EO 30cm shows compound intact, walled perimeter. New 12m antenna mast erected on roof of main building, visible in panchromatic. Two military-type pickups (likely technicals) parked inside courtyard; third vehicle near main gate. No visible UAS or missile launchers. Port administration building 260m south shows no vehicle activity or external hardening. No recent battle damage observed on compound or surrounding structures.

CDF command net geolocated to compound on 9 of 10 days since 01OCT26. Net active primarily 0600-0900Z and 1600-2000Z. Callsigns 'SHARIF-6' and 'BAHR-2' used for C2. Short transmission bursts on secondary net from Perim Island relay. 071600Z burst of 54 sec on UHF, encrypted, associated with compound. No change in net pattern detected.

Six nights continuous FMV 06-11OCT26 shows compound activity peak 1700-0300Z. Nightly 2-3 vehicles arrive between 1800-2000Z, depart between 0100-0300Z. Personnel observed on rooftop at irregular intervals (15-45 min) throughout night, likely lookouts. Lights in main building constant; antenna mast lit by small red beacon. No civilian traffic within 200m of compound walls. Port admin building dark and unoccupied all nights.

T-07s.name: Houthi UAF command cell (3rd floor, mixed-use building)
T-07s.function: Reported command-and-control cell for Unmanned Air Force operations against shipping
T-07s.effect: Destroy 3rd-floor command cell during reported meeting

intel.source: YM-HS-2261 (C3: fairly reliable / possibly true; first reporting on this subject; sub-source access indirect)
intel.text: Source's relative, who works as a driver in Shu'ub, states that 'men from the drone command' meet on the third floor of the building above the pharmacy on Sundays, Tuesdays and Thursdays in the morning, 'around ten'. Sub-source did not enter the building and could not name any attendee. Source has not previously reported on Houthi UAF matters.

A handset previously associated with a mid-level UAF officer was active in Shu'ub district on 3 of the last 5 days, mornings. Geolocation is cell-level only (approx. 1.2 km radius); no fix to a specific building. No UAF C2 traffic attributed to the location.

Four-story mixed-use building on a commercial street. Pharmacy and phone shop at ground level; laundry and children's clothing visible on upper-floor balconies. Two SUVs parked outside at 1015L. No antennas, guards or military vehicles observed. Girls' primary school 45 m E (courtyard, ~400 pupils at recess). MoPHP health center 70 m S. Street stalls along the block.

intel.source: Limited: 2 days of intermittent EO; no persistent ISR allocated
intel.text: Families observed entering and leaving upper floors throughout both days. School in session 0730-1230L Sun-Thu. Health center queue 30-60 people mid-morning. Could not confirm or deny meetings on the 3rd floor. CCJ2 requested persistent ISR (not yet allocated).

T-08.name: Coastal artillery / ASCM firing positions
T-08.location: South-west ridge, Perim (Mayun) Island, Bab al-Mandab
T-08.function: Dug-in firing positions overlooking the Bab al-Mandab traffic separation scheme
T-08.effect: Destroy firing positions and ammunition bunker

intel.source: YM-HS-1108 (B2, reliability assessed B3 via YEM GOL liaison)
intel.text: Source, a former Perim resident, confirms Houthi CDF personnel occupy four dug-in positions on the SW ridge overlooking the old airstrip. An ammunition bunker is located approximately 70 meters from a caretaker family's occupied building in the abandoned residential compound. Source reports daily maintenance of artillery pieces and one TEL during daylight hours. Source observed increased activity following the 05 Oct surface attack.

Imagery identifies four separate, revetted firing positions on the SW ridge, each containing a single artillery piece. One position contains a TEL. A hardened ammunition bunker is visible 70 meters south of a two-story residential building, the only intact structure in a compound otherwise in ruin. No civilian activity observed near positions at time of tasking. Former airstrip surface partially obscured by camouflage netting.

Detected Houthi CDF fire-control net, callsigns 'SHARK' and 'BARGE' on VHF low band. Traffic profile indicates routine radio checks at dawn and dusk, with spikes in activity following naval transits through Bab al-Mandab. Intercepts on 08 Oct include grid coordinate corrections consistent with targeting reference points near TSS separation zone. No additional nets identified. Reporting is fragmentary due to terrain shielding.

FMV over six consecutive nights shows consistent activity pattern: personnel leave dug-in positions at 1800 local, move to the residential compound building for evening meal, and return by 1930. One or two personnel remain at positions overnight as sentries. Ammunition bunker is accessed only between 0600-0700 hours, with personnel carrying crates to positions. TEL is hidden under camouflage netting during daylight, uncovered only during 0400-0500 maintenance window.
